name: mapforge
about: MapForge: pixel-art map generator, tile editor and figure builder with Godot 4 export. Coordinates are tile cells (x to the right, y down, 0-based). A cell value is a tile gid (0 = empty); gids come from list_tiles. Typical flow: status → new_map (or generate) → render to look at it → paint / place_object / copy_paste to edit → render again → export_godot. Own tilesets: tileset_add → tileset_render → tileset_assign → generate. Figures: figure_parts → figure_set_part / figure_color → figure_draw for own pixels → figure_render → figure_export_godot.

commands.name: status
commands.description: Current project: size, view, seed, layers (with tile counts), objects, rooms, undo state, current page.

commands.name: new_map
commands.description: Create a new map project and generate it (like the setup wizard). The current project is saved first. The map is saved as a project of its own; the user sees it in MapForge under Karte → „Gespeicherte Karten“ (badge „KI“). With the local server's hidden browser the maps move into the user's MapForge tab as soon as the user opens it.

perspective.description: Optional exact perspective (top_down view: top_down or low_top_down)

mode.description: manual = empty map to paint by hand

commands.name: generate
commands.description: Generate the map again with the current settings (same seed = same map, new_seed = a new variant).

commands.name: get_generator
commands.description: Generator settings of the project (rooms, corridors, terrain, objects, side-scroller / hex options).

commands.name: set_generator
commands.description: Change generator settings (deep merge of `patch`, same shape as get_generator). regenerate=true generates right away. layout: rooms | cave | outdoor (forest clearings + dirt paths) | village (outdoor + houses + well) | island (land in the sea with beaches); houses (true: houses also for outdoor/island); rivers 0-2 (outdoor layouts, bridges over paths); climate summer | winter | desert (outdoor layouts); caveRoughness 0-100; look {softEdges, floorPatches, smartDeco, smoothRooms} (all true by default).

commands.name: list_tiles
commands.description: Tiles usable in this map with gid, role, category and tags. Filter by role / category / tag (substring match).

commands.name: tileset_list
commands.description: Tilesets of the project: id, name, tile size, gid range, number of tiles, active, perspectives, how many tiles are assigned / still unconfirmed suggestions. Also the allowed categories and roles for tileset_assign.

commands.name: tileset_add
commands.description: Add an own tileset from a PNG (url or base64). Clean grids are cut as they are, sheets of separate pieces (gaps, different sizes, AI-generated sheets) are cut into their pieces automatically; then every tile gets an automatic suggestion (floor, wall, corner …). tile_size forces a plain grid of that size. For sheets with gaps set tile_width / tile_height (non-square allowed), margin (border around the sheet) and spacing (gap between tiles) like in Tiled – the sheet is repacked into a tight square grid.

url.description: https address of a PNG (the server must allow the download – CORS)

image_base64.description: PNG as base64 (not via the phone relay for big images)

perspectives.description: map kinds the tileset is drawn for (empty = all)

commands.name: tileset_render
commands.description: Picture of a tileset with every tile's gid and its current assignment (short label; '?' = unconfirmed suggestion) – to see what the tiles are before assigning them. Big tilesets: look at a band of rows with row / rows and col / cols (e.g. 12×12 tiles at a time) so the gids stay readable.

commands.name: tileset_assign
commands.description: Assign tiles (like correcting them in the palette): category, role (auto-tiling), tags, collision. Several gids at once. Confirms suggestions; the app learns from it for future tilesets.

commands.name: tileset_auto_assign
commands.description: Automatic assignment again for all tiles that are not confirmed yet (confirmed / edited tiles stay). confirm=true accepts all suggestions afterwards.

commands.name: tileset_update
commands.description: Rename a tileset, switch it on / off (active = used by the generator and the palette), or set the map kinds it is for.

commands.name: tileset_recut
commands.description: Cut a tileset anew from its original image: tile size, non-square tiles, margin and spacing. Placed tiles of this tileset are removed (the gids change); assignments are suggested again.

commands.name: tileset_mark_room
commands.description: Fastest way to set up an own tileset: frame a drawn sample room in the tileset picture (tile columns/rows, see tileset_render). The frame's corners become outer corners, its edges walls (top/bottom/left/right), the inside floor; with front_rows the rows under the top edge become wall fronts (3/4 view). By default the automatic suggestions of all other tiles are dropped, so only the framed tiles build rooms.

front_rows.description: rows of wall front under the top edge (0 = flat walls)

clear_others.description: drop automatic suggestions of the other tiles (default true)

commands.name: tileset_remove
commands.description: Remove an own (uploaded) tileset; its tiles disappear from the map (undo possible).

commands.name: list_layers
commands.description: Layers from bottom to top with id, name, role, visibility, lock, opacity, tile count.

commands.name: get_map
commands.description: Cell values of an area (max 64 × 64) per layer as rows of numbers (gid, 0 = empty; values ≥ 268435456 carry rotate/mirror bits). Also the blocked (collision) grid as '#' / '.'.

layers.description: Layer names, ids or roles (default: all with content)

commands.name: paint
commands.description: Paint a tile into a layer at cells and / or a rectangle – one undo step. Auto-walls re-tile walls around painted floor / paths (default on). rotate / mirror turn the tile.

layer.description: Layer name, id or role (default: active layer)

commands.name: fill
commands.description: Flood fill from (x, y) in a layer with a tile (like the fill bucket).

commands.name: clear_area
commands.description: Clear a rectangle on all unlocked layers including objects (one undo step).

commands.name: copy_paste
commands.description: Copy a rectangle (all layers, objects, structure) and stamp it at to_x / to_y (top-left). Empty cells keep what is below. Optional rotate (90 steps) / mirror.

commands.name: list_objects
commands.description: Objects on the map (id, type, x = left cell, y = base row) and the object types that can be placed.

commands.name: place_object
commands.description: Place an object (tree, pine, palm, pillar, rock, arch, chest, merchant, house, well, or an own object id from figure_to_map). x = left cell of its footprint, y = the row it stands on.

commands.name: remove_object
commands.description: Remove an object by id (see list_objects).

commands.name: set_layer
commands.description: Change a layer: visible, locked, opacity (0.1–1, editor only), name, or make it the active layer.

commands.name: undo
commands.description: Undo the last change(s).

commands.name: redo
commands.description: Redo undone change(s).

commands.name: render
commands.description: Picture of the map (or an area) as PNG, like in the editor incl. objects. Use it to look at your work. tile_px = pixels per tile (default: fits 1024 px).

commands.name: export_godot
commands.description: Godot 4 package of the map as a ZIP (map.json, loader script, tilesets, player figure, Map.tscn) – returned base64 (the MCP server saves it to `path`).

commands.name: export_json
commands.description: The map as MapForge/Godot JSON (tiles per layer, collision rects, rooms, spawn points, objects) without images.

commands.name: save
commands.description: Save the project in the browser now (it also autosaves).

commands.name: list_projects
commands.description: Saved map projects in this browser. ai=true marks maps made by an AI.

commands.name: open_project
commands.description: Open a saved project by id (see list_projects).

commands.name: style_colors
commands.description: The look of the project's tiles: most used colours (with share %), the darkest (outline) colour and the tile size. Use it before drawing figures for a map so they match its style.

commands.name: level_list
commands.description: The levels (Ebenen) of the project – floors of a dungeon, a cellar … Each level is a map of its own; all map commands work on the open level. Tilesets and own objects are shared.

commands.name: level_add
commands.description: Add a level with the map settings of the open one and open it (generates it unless generate=false). Use for several floors / areas the user asks for.

commands.name: level_switch
commands.description: Open another level (id, name or number from level_list).

commands.name: figure_status
commands.description: The figure in the builder (character, creature or object): name, size (pixels, square), layers (id, slot, part, drawn, own_views), colours and the anatomy – where head, torso, arms, legs (character), body, eyes, ground (creature) or the bounds (object) sit in pixel coordinates of this view, so own drawings line up with the parts and animate correctly, and its animations (built-in and own).

commands.name: figure_draw
commands.description: Draw own pixels onto a figure layer – for details and shapes no part has (emblems, belts, masks, special armour, horns, a whole creature or object). rows = picture lines, one character per pixel, starting at x/y; palette maps each character to a colour ('#rrggbb', '#rrggbbaa' or 'none' = erase). '.' and space leave a pixel unchanged. Without layer a new layer is made in slot (default 'extra'); the slot decides how animations move it and the drawing order. Each view (front, fside, side, bside, back) has its own pixels: draw the views that differ; views never drawn show the front pixels unless hide_in_other_views is true (then they stay empty there – good for front-only details like a chest emblem). Drawing on a part layer keeps its other views. mirror: also paints the mirrored pixel (symmetric front views: draw the left half). clear: empty this view of the layer first.

layer.description: id or name of an existing layer (figure_status); omit for a new layer

slot.description: slot of a new layer (see figure_parts), default extra

commands.name: figure_grid
commands.description: The figure (or one layer) of a view as text pixels: rows + palette + x/y of the top left corner, cropped to what is drawn – the same format figure_draw takes. Use it to edit exact pixels.

commands.name: figure_anim_frames
commands.description: One frame of an animation of the figure as text pixels (rows + palette + x/y), plus frame count, fps and frame size. Built-in animations (walk, idle, attack, k_hop … – see figure_status) are computed from the figure's parts; own animations come from figure_anim_new. Frames are bigger than the figure (room for jumps and swings): the figure sits figure_offset pixels in.

commands.name: figure_anim_draw
commands.description: Change pixels of one animation frame (same text format as figure_draw; coordinates in the frame). For built-in animations this overrides the computed frame (reset: true goes back to the automatic one); own animations are changed directly. Use it to let capes, tails, hair or wings follow the motion, fix a weapon, add effects (dust, sparks, magic).

rows.description: lines of the picture, one character per pixel ('.' = unchanged)

commands.name: figure_anim_new
commands.description: Create an own animation (e.g. cast a spell, dodge, dance, sleep, open): frames start as copies of an existing animation (from) or of the standing figure; then change them frame by frame with figure_anim_draw. It is exported to Godot with the figure.

from.description: animation to start from (id), else the standing figure

commands.name: figure_parts
commands.description: Building parts for a figure kind, grouped by slot (body, hair, top, weapon …) with id and label; also the colour channels and their presets.

commands.name: figure_set_part
commands.description: Put a part on the figure (replaces the part in its slot, or adds for multi slots). Parts fit the body automatically.

commands.name: figure_remove_slot
commands.description: Remove the layer(s) of a slot from the figure.

commands.name: figure_color
commands.description: Set a colour channel (skin, hair, primary, secondary, metal, wood, stone, leaf) – either a preset index or 3 hex colours [light, base, dark].

commands.name: figure_new
commands.description: Start a new figure: random parts, or empty (a blank canvas for drawing it yourself with figure_draw). size in pixels (default 32; parts are made for 32, larger sizes centre them).

commands.name: figure_random
commands.description: Roll random parts and colours for the figure.

commands.name: figure_render
commands.description: Picture of the figure as PNG – one view or all views side by side; optionally an animation as a strip of frames.

animation.description: animation id or own animation (see figure_status → animations)

commands.name: figure_save
commands.description: Save the figure to the gallery.

commands.name: figure_export_godot
commands.description: Godot package of the figure with animations as ZIP (base64; the MCP server saves it to `path`). directions: 2 (platformer), 4 or 8.

commands.name: figure_use_as_player
commands.description: Use the character / creature as the player figure in the playtest and in the map's Godot export.

commands.name: figure_to_map
commands.description: Put the figure (front view) into the current map as an own object type (id own_…); then place it with place_object. Updating the figure and calling this again updates the object.

commands.name: show
commands.description: Switch the visible page of the app (map, figures, project) so the user sees what you do.
